preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the RSQ uncertainty band, the fixed 0.3 mm/h structural term, and the "Δ WITHIN UNCERTAINTY" qualifier verbatim; they convert a vendor-family offset into an explicitly nullified number the drainage-planning committee can read and defer. Because the band's inputs are residual calibration uncertainties that creep between certificate renewals, I mandate that any comparison cell whose residual was last renewed more than fourteen days before the shared-event instant expands the printed band by (trailing-30-day drift-slope × days-since-renewal) and appends "STALE CAL — BAND EXPANDED [+N d × slope]" alongside the base figure. The failure this closes: Site 7's week-10 delta of 1.2 mm/h exceeds the stale week-4 band of 1.06 mm/h and prints as a resolvable divergence, scoping a catch-basin upsizing against Site 7's culvert, while the true band incorporating six weeks of 0.04 mm/h/week creep computes to 1.31 mm/h and nullifies the divergence entirely. The staleness annotation, carrying the slope value and the renewal-date gap, lets a year-three appendix reader reconstruct that the "resolvable" figure was an artifact of delayed metrology service rather than a validated spatial signal, preserving the uncertainty budget's auditability without silently discarding the nullification.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the trailing-30-day drift-slope expansion and the "STALE CAL — BAND EXPANDED" annotation verbatim; they make the nullification auditable to the metrology-service delay rather than to the spatial signal. Because a trailing-30-day slope estimate is itself vulnerable to short-duration environmental stress, I mandate that the operative slope be computed over a rolling 90-day window and that any divergence between the 30-day and 90-day slopes exceeding 50 % triggers the larger (conservative) slope with an appended "SLOPE DISAGREEMENT — CONSERVATIVE EXPANSION APPLIED" tag carrying both slope values and their respective window dates. The failure this closes: Site 8's two-week hail-event series mechanically stressed the gauge tip, inflating the 30-day slope to +0.12 mm/h/week against a true 90-day slope of +0.03 mm/h/week, and the over-expanded band nullifies a genuine 1.5 mm/h week-14 structural offset arising from Site 8's drainage-adjacent placement, deferring a legitimate culvert-sizing correction through another month of decaying hail-stress artifact. I therefore require that the conservative-slope annotation permits a year-three appendix reader to reconstruct the hail-stress transient and the underlying structural offset as independent causal variables rather than to read a single inflated number that conflates both.

target.speaker: X
target.text: I adopt the 90-day rolling slope, the 50 % disagreement trigger, and the conservative-expansion-with-dual-slope annotation verbatim; they let a year-three reader attribute week-14's inflated band to the hail-stress transient rather than to the underlying structural offset. Because the conservative slope is a one-way ratchet that decays as hail weeks age out of the 30-day window, I mandate that any comparison cell whose status flips between "Δ WITHIN UNCERTAINTY" and a resolved numeric delta across consecutive weeks carries a bold "BAND STATUS TRANSITION — WITHIN→ABOVE" (or reverse) annotation logging the slope-window aging vector—which specific event-weeks aged out, which new weeks entered, and the resulting slope delta—so the transition is attributable to statistical-window dynamics. The failure this closes: the identical Site-8 drainage-adjacent structural offset of 1.5 mm/h prints "WITHIN UNCERTAINTY" under the expanded week-14 band but flips to a resolved numeric delta by week-22 when the hail-stress transients age out and the 30-day slope converges to the tighter 90-day value; without the transition annotation a drainage-planning committee member comparing the two weeks' printed cells reads the status flip as evidence that the physical configuration changed—triggering an urgent re-survey of Site-8's culvert geometry—when in fact only the statistical lens contracted around an invariant signal. The aging-vector annotation, naming the exact hail-event weeks that exited the window, lets the committee defer the re-survey to the scheduled quarterly geometry audit rather than dispatching an emergency crew to verify a structure that never moved.
